judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is a statutory disclosure notice reciting the TRIA definition of terrorism; the definition is long but tracks the statute and names its certifying officials.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the policy 'makes available' terrorism insurance while c005 states the terrorism premium is $-0-, a mild recital/operative tension, but no coverage section turns on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain statement of the federal reimbursement formula with a fixed percentage; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c003 and c004 on the Treasury cap and with the Declarations; no operative conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains an OCR-style run-together ('ina Program Year') but the meaning of the $100 billion cap is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside c004, which repeats the same cap from the insurer's side, and the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear statement of the insurer's cap and pro rata allocation keyed to the Act; no vague operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Harmonises with c003 and with the general limit-of-liability provisions; no contrary clause located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single figure ('$ -0-') with no ambiguity in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A zero terrorism premium can be read against c001's statement that terrorism insurance is 'made available', but the notice is disclosure, not an operative grant of coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure informational notice about producer compensation; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses producer compensation, so no conflict exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward statement that three named coverage sections are claims-made; the terms are defined by reference elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: None of the three named sections (Executive Liability, EPL, Fiduciary) was purchased — Item 3 lists only General Terms, Crime and Special Coverage — so the notice is orphaned within the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional and self-limiting ('if a claims-made coverage section contains a retroactive date'); little to argue about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No retroactive or prior acts date appears anywhere in the attached Crime declarations, making the notice inert rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes the claims-made trigger in generic terms; 'incidents reported' is loose but is descriptive notice language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime Coverage Section is a discovery-based, not claims-made, section, so this notice cannot be applied to the coverage actually purchased.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sets specific periods (sixty days automatic, one year optional) and is self-explanatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to extended reporting periods for coverage sections not included in this policy, and no ERP provision appears in the Crime section or General Terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: General market commentary about premium levels with an obvious typographical error ('matunity') that does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Not an operative term and unconnected to any pricing provision elsewhere in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A capitalised declarations warning; 'WHICHEVER ARE PURCHASED' hedges its application and the defined terms are quoted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It warns about defence costs eroding limits although the only purchased sections (Crime, Special Coverage) contain no defence-cost mechanism, an untidy but hedged fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration/preamble language; nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It subordinates the General Terms to the Declarations and other terms, consistent with c015's priority rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Coverage shall extend anywhere in the world' is an extremely short, absolute phrase whose reach against coverage-specific geographic limits is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime section contains geographically bounded terms — Premises, Banking Premises, and counterfeit 'United States of America or Canadian paper currency' in c078 — so worldwide territory and those limits must be reconciled by c015's control rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conflict-resolution rule stated in ordinary terms; 'inconsistent or in conflict' is broad but is the standard formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the provision a court would use to resolve tensions such as the worldwide territory clause versus the Crime section's limits, and it does not itself contradict anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer definition with no substantive content of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime section defines no 'Claim' at all, so notice provisions keyed to a Claim (c021) have no anchor for this coverage section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference; the meaning is supplied elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Crime c074 supplies a definition of Insured, so the referral works, though Insured and Organization are used inconsistently across the insuring clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the Parent Organization by reference to Item 1; entirely determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 1 names Medidata Solutions Inc., matching the Crime declarations; no discrepancy found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by reference to Item 2 with a proportionality rule; clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Crime c116 and Endorsement 3 (c130), which shift the trigger from loss sustained during the Policy Period to loss Discovered during it, but the definition itself remains stable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States that limits and retentions are separate unless stated to the contrary; mechanical and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Crime c116's per-clause limits and c057's no-retention rule for expenses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed address and effectiveness rules; the final saving sentence ('not reasonably possible') is a familiar standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Endorsement/Rider 1 (c039-c041), which adds a prejudice requirement, and with Crime c118, which makes 90-day notice a condition precedent — a genuine three-way tension over late notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specifies currency, source of exchange rate and the valuation date for each situation; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Crime c119 contains its own valuation and foreign-currency rules keyed to the Discovery date, and this clause expressly yields ('Except as otherwise provided in any coverage section').

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional subrogation and cooperation language; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with Crime c120 (Recoveries), which allocates recoveries after payment; no contradiction identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full compliance with all the terms' as a condition precedent is broad, and the judgment-based direct-action mechanics are drafted for third-party liability coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applied to the first-party Crime section, the unsatisfied-judgment machinery has no work to do, and the strict compliance condition sits against Endorsement 1's prejudice rule (c039).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed agency clause with an express carve-out for Extended Reporting Period notices; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out references an ERP that no purchased coverage section provides, a small orphan reference; otherwise consistent with c112's ERISA payment-holding rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-oral-modification and anti-assignment clause naming the required signatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsements in the file are so signed, consistent with this requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed 20-day notice period tied to a fixed 60-day window; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads coherently with the rest of Subsection 11 and with c035's requirement that notice state reasons.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated closed list of statutory cancellation grounds; 'substantially and materially increases the hazard' is a standard regulatory phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The listed grounds track New York law and do not conflict with the other termination triggers in Subsection 11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple effective-date rule for insured-initiated termination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dovetails with the short-rate refund rule in c032; no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line mutual-agreement termination trigger; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other enumerated termination routes in Subsection 11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Expiration and nonrenewal stated by reference to Item 2 and paragraph (g); clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to paragraph (g) (c033) is accurate and the two operate together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Customary short rates' is undefined and imports an extrinsic industry practice, which gives some room for argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision defines short rates or premium refunds, so nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long and intricate but each step is tied to specific day counts and defined triggers; 'incomplete or late' notice is the softest term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its limit-increase rule interacts with c019's proportional-limit sentence and c116's limits, but the two can be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Administrative copy-to-broker requirement; nothing capable of dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the notice provisions in c033 and c035.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires reasons and effective date in a notice; determinate obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the reason-specific requirements of c028 and c033.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Terminates scheduled prior bonds as of inception; clear and self-executing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Crime c115's prior-bond termination language, and c129 deletes Subsection 24 entirely, leaving prior-loss treatment governed only here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard bankruptcy-does-not-relieve clause; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses insolvency of an Insured, so no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headings-are-not-operative boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated in every endorsement (c044, c123, c126), consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Introduces a prejudice requirement with a carve-out to paragraph (2); 'prejudiced the Company' is a legal standard rather than a vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It softens the strict notice conditions in GTC c021 and Crime c118's 'condition precedent' 90-day rule, so the interaction of the three must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not reasonably possible' and 'as soon as reasonably possible' are elastic but conventional standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the last paragraph of GTC c021 almost verbatim, so it reinforces rather than contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates burden by a bright-line two-year period and lists two irrebuttable-presumption triggers; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c039's prejudice framework; the suit limitation in c118 uses a different two-year measure but on a different subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A saving clause limiting how the endorsement may be construed; broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the claims-made structure of sections not purchased here, a mild orphan reference within this policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Relies on 'death or personal injury, as that term is defined by the New York Insurance Law', an express external referent that narrows the phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants a direct action notwithstanding c024's bar on joining the Company, which c024 does not carve out — a tension resolved only by the 'notwithstanding any other provision' language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate on headings and unchanged terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'all other terms remain unchanged' formula is repeated across endorsements that amend the same Exclusion 19, but this instance is not itself the conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other similar laws or regulations' is an open-ended catch-all appended to 'trade or economic sanctions', a classic general-versus-specific scope problem, and 'to the extent that' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses sanctions, so the exclusion stands alone without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headings and unchanged-terms boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the identical formula elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consideration preamble subjecting the Crime section to the Declarations and General Terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Squares with c015's rule that a coverage section controls over inconsistent General Terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Direct loss' and 'resulting from' are causation words that insurers and insureds routinely read differently, though the clause is otherwise tight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is amended for ERISA losses by c112 and cut back by c103/c104's exclusions, all of which are expressly cross-referenced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Uses 'direct loss' and layers sub-items (i)-(iv) with a trailing 'committed by a Third Party' whose reach across the list is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusions c105 and c106 carve back this clause expressly, and the Premises definition (c081) bounds it; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same structure as the Premises clause, with a trailing 'committed by a Third Party' qualifier of uncertain reach over items (i) and (ii).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the In Transit definition (c075) and exclusions c105(b) and c102, it is coherent.
